entry.title: Narrow the "no dialogue" claim so that it is literally true
entry.content:
Narrow the "no dialogue" claim so that it is literally true

Every README and notice said no repository here reproduces "a line of
dialogue". Auditing the published data against that sentence found it was
99.94% true rather than 100%: of 15,867 headwords, 14 are clause-shaped and
five of those are verbatim short lines from the show (the worst being an
11-word pun).

The claims that were already exact are kept, and they carry the message:
no subtitle file, no transcript, no timing data, no example sentence, no
dialogue translation. What is dropped is only the absolute that overstated
the case. The headword bullet now reads "a word, a fixed phrase, or a short
situational expression", which describes what the data actually holds.

Applied in the generator so all three corpora and all seven languages move
together, and in the profile README in both languages.

Found by asking the opposite question of the one the release audit asks. The
audit looks for a leaked example sentence and passes; nobody had checked
whether the entries that legitimately have no example field might still be
sentences themselves.

Also fixes two layout defects in the generated NOTICE: a heading that ran
straight on from the preceding paragraph, and a line wrap that produced a
one-word line.

entry.title: Build the corpus repositories, and add a matrix-wide validator
entry.content:
Build the corpus repositories, and add a matrix-wide validator

Adds the machinery for the rest of the matrix, and fixes three defects found
while using it.

Corpus repositories
- tools/corpus_i18n/ — a compact README template in 7 languages, plus per-show
  prose. The corpus README is a data page, not a manifesto, so it stays short.
- tools/build_corpus_docs.py — puts READMEs, LICENSE (CC BY 4.0 with the
  attribution wording spelled out), NOTICE.md and .gitignore next to the
  exported data. `build_corpora.py` now runs it, so one command produces a
  repository that can be pushed.
- The per-show figures come from matrix.json like everywhere else. A language
  module never contains a number.

Defects fixed on the way
- Corpus READMEs named `data/anki/nypd-blue-safe.csv`; the exporter writes
  `anki-nypd-blue-safe.csv`. A reader's first action would have failed. The
  generator now resolves the real filenames from the slug, and `--check` fails
  if a README ever names a file that is not on disk.
- `grab export --format md|html` labelled everything in Chinese — table
  headers, the search placeholder, the footer — in data files published to
  seven language groups. Structural labels are now English
  (Headword/Gloss/IPA), matching the `TV Vocab` deck-name decision. The gloss
  content stays Chinese; that is data, and it is the top contribution ask.
- A repair queue below 100 rows is no longer published. Three leftover rows
  invite nobody to contribute, and an undocumented file in a public repository
  is worse than no file. The rows stay in the master workspace.

New: tools/validate_matrix.py
The only check that sees what no single repository can see about itself —
whether every repository links to every other one, whether any relative link
resolves, whether the language bars are complete, whether any figure in prose
has gone stale, and whether anything private reached any of them. The profile
node is satisfied by either the profile repository or the profile page, since
the repository is what GitHub renders at that page.

Release checklist updated to run it. All five repositories pass: 0 errors.

entry.title: grab-series-vocab: an agent skill that builds a deduplicated TV vocab…
entry.content:
grab-series-vocab: an agent skill that builds a deduplicated TV vocabulary corpus

Turn a directory of subtitle files into a searchable vocabulary library
(headword, gloss, IPA, difficulty) that exports to Anki, Markdown, or a
single-file web page.

The design decision that shapes everything: build the corpus first and treat
every export as a view of it. A per-episode pipeline re-collects what it has
already seen -- measured on 33,270 cards, 35.9% were duplicates, and duplicate
cards are not merely wasted effort, they corrupt the review schedule.

Architecture
- library-first: one SQLite corpus, exports are views
- schema-first: every ingested row is validated against entry.schema.json
- deduplication by construction: the existing headwords are emitted as a
  blocklist before any agent work is dispatched
- two export modes: `full` keeps the example sentence for local study,
  `safe` drops it. Only `safe` is ever published.

Contents
- skills/grab-series-vocab/  the skill (SKILL.md, schema, references, CLI)
- tools/                     matrix.json as the single source of figures,
                             7-language README generator, corpus builder,
                             legacy importer, doc-figure sync, release audit
- examples/demo/             fictional bilingual sample + expected output
- docs/                      install, study method, pipeline, matrix map,
                             corpus catalogue

README in English, 中文, Español, 日本語, 한국어, Deutsch, Français.

No subtitle text is published anywhere. tools/audit_public.py enforces that:
it fails the build on a dialogue-bearing key in a published JSONL, on a
subtitle cue timestamp, or on an English sentence sitting in a definition
column, and it reads private terms from a gitignored local list rather than
hard-coding them in the check itself.

MIT. Vocabulary data in the companion corpora is CC BY 4.0.
